# Phase Two — Gevurah Critique

The Awtsmoos is not impressed by motion without measure;
Awtsmoos.com becomes cleaner when each tempting shortcut is cut away like false treasure.

## Twenty improvements to Phase One

1. Do not assume `modules/player/core.js` creates visible controls; trace DOM ownership first.
2. Do not rewrite root `style.css` until the import/load graph proves it is authoritative.
3. Treat generated style strings as code debt, but rewrite only their full owner files.
4. Separate player/media work from studio/editor work so one wave remains reviewable.
5. Establish a Rebbe-local layer scale before changing any numeric z-index.
6. Map every fixed element's anchor edge so bottom collisions are solved as a system.
7. Preserve hidden native file inputs where semantically useful; style their trigger, not the hidden input.
8. Treat range/color/checkbox controls as intentional studio primitives with route-local classes.
9. Avoid one universal control selector that accidentally restyles modal/search/player controls alike.
10. Prefer `:focus-visible` over generic focus chrome while retaining accessible keyboard evidence.
11. Ensure fine-pointer hover is gated so touch does not emulate hover incorrectly.
12. Give active/pressed feedback to all primary buttons, including generated search/playlist actions.
13. Add reduced-motion handling to every newly animated interactive surface.
14. Keep modal content scrolling inside bounded shells at short viewport heights.
15. Replace 100vw/100vh overlays with logical inset + dvh/safe-area where appropriate.
16. Prevent sticky headers from stacking above truly modal surfaces via named tokens.
17. Prevent download notifications from competing with bottom player controls.
18. Check line length and line count before testing, not after broad test success.
19. Modernize stale tests only when Git-clean and proven obsolete by current architecture.
20. Update REMAINING_WORK after each closure/discovery rather than waiting for a final report.

## Risk graph

Duplicate CSS -> cascade conflict -> false visual fixes.
Inline generated CSS -> hidden specificity -> mobile regressions.
Raw z-index -> overlay wars -> unreachable controls.
Fixed bottom UI -> player/download/selection collisions.
Native media -> branded visual rupture.
Studio controls -> inconsistent browser defaults.
Large legacy files -> unsafe rewrites -> require modular extraction.
